question: Does the swap target's answer appear when the bridge's representation is swapped for the target's, and does that depend on the J-space part of the representation?
swap: clamp.SwapClamp at every band layer, positions 1.. (not 0); atoms per condition as in the script docstring; unit atoms throughout
eligibility: answer and swap answer have single-token surfaces; both entities have probes; clean answer at word rank 1 (formatting tokens excluded)
flip: swap answer at word rank 1 after the swap (strictly: no other word scores as high)
metrics: share keeping the clean answer at rank 1, Wilson 95% CI

decision.labels: 2x2 on (jpart flips, remainder_clamped flips): J-mediated = (True, False), non-J = (False, True), both = (True, True), neither = (False, False)

deviations: Items whose answer or swap answer has no single-token surface are dropped and counted (7 of 90 at setup).

Edit size is the direct edit at the final position, |delta| / |h|, averaged over the edited band layers per item and reported as the median over items; the edit's downstream effect on later layers is not measured.
Layers where the two swapped atoms are near-parallel (|cos| > 0.999) are skipped and counted.

Word rank is strict: an exact logit tie with another word ranks a candidate 2nd, so a flip and a kept clean answer exclude each other (gate and gate_w1 counted ties as rank 1 for both: 2 and 3 of 528 outcomes).

Null direction: one random unit direction per (item, condition, layer), shared across positions and scaled to each position's own edit norm, so it matches the real edit, which lies in one fixed low-dimensional span at every position.
The band was picked by gate gate_v3 on these same items, so full_probe's rate is optimistic.
Gate gate_v3 failed (full probe 27% < 30%), and so did the two before it (gate 17%, gate_w1 8%). The plan says stop and debug; the human chose to run main anyway.
